newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends on five-month high, awaits stock.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends on five-month high, awaits stock.

text.p: COMEX copper ended at a five month high ahead of Tuesday's LME inventory report as the market appeared to shrug off any lingering belief in the existence of huge, off-exchange stocks, traders and analysts said.
Some brokers expected LME stocks to dip below 100,000 tonnes Tuesday to their lowest level in more than six years.
"Copper prices have recovered dramatically to over 100 cents to reflect what's happening in visible inventories," said Vahid Fahti of Everen Securities.

The big drawdowns in LME stocks was for consumption, especially in China. "The Chinese are savvy buyers. I think what's not appreciated in the copper market is the strength of demand," Fahti said. "We strongly disagree that the decline in inventory was not fundamental."
December COMEX copper settled 4.20 cents firmer at 105.65 cents per pound, traded 105.90 to 100.80 cents, building on a 5.60-cent gain Friday.
But volume on Monday was not particularly heavy, estimated at 16,000 lots compared to Friday's official 18,465 lots.
LME three months rose to a five-month high of $2,200 a tonne in evening trading, with a $120 cash to threes premium.
